rationale:
TRIAGE: All three candidates merit close downstream comparison because they represent two distinct endpoint definitions and two sibling models with near-identical reported performance.

- PGS001033 is the only candidate directly aligned to the target trait EFO (blood coagulation disease) via its reported endpoint “Other coagulation defects (time-to-event)”. It also provides cleaner, directly comparable discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R² and full-model AUROC with CIs) and a larger validation N (67,425). Even though it is a different phenotype label than the congenital-deficiency endpoint, it is the strongest “direct-endpoint with explicit predictive evidence” option and could be favored if endpoint fidelity to the target is prioritized.

- PGS001826 and PGS002034 are same-publication siblings targeting “Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)” (different EFO than the target). They have very similar partial correlation estimates (~0.0562 vs ~0.0563 with overlapping CIs), same training size and validation setup, and conventional covariates. Because their metrics are not AUROC/R² and are reported as partial-r, a single-shot picker could be misled by metric incomparability versus PGS001033; they should be kept for head-to-head comparison both against each other (near-tie) and against PGS001033 (endpoint-alignment vs metric/packaging differences).

- Between the siblings, PGS002034 (LDpred2; 32,552 variants) vs PGS001826 (penalized regression; 45 variants) is a classic “dense vs sparse” contrast with essentially identical reported partial-r. Either could win depending on downstream preferences (e.g., implementation simplicity vs potential robustness), so both should remain in the close-compare set rather than prematurely selecting one. Uncertainty: Cross-candidate performance comparability is limited because PGS001033 reports AUROC/R² (including PRS-only), while PGS001826/PGS002034 report partial correlation only; without a shared metric axis, the apparent strength of PGS001033 vs the congenital-deficiency siblings cannot be cleanly adjudicated at triage. Endpoint alignment also differs (time-to-event ‘other coagulation defects’ vs congenital deficiency), so downstream comparison should explicitly separate (a) endpoint fidelity to the target EFO and (b) strength/cleanliness of predictive evidence. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All three candidates are only partial direct matches to the broad target “blood coagulation disease.” PGS001033 maps to the target EFO and has the closest broad coagulation-disease framing, but its phenotyping is time-to-event (“TTE other coagulation defects”) and it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-PRS framework paper, which domain guidance flags as a generalization risk. The two alternatives (PGS001826, PGS002034) are for a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency endpoint (different EFO) and report only partial-correlation metrics (no AUROC/R2), with additional covariate packaging (birth date, deprivation index) that reduces comparability. Given these tradeoffs and limited comparable performance evidence across models, PGS001033 is the best-supported direct-match option available, but overall evidence is insufficient for a high-quality direct recommendation. PICK: Keep the legacy proposal. Among the full candidate list, PGS001033 is the only record whose trait_efo directly matches the target (“blood coagulation disease”) and its reported phenotype (“TTE other coagulation defects”) is the closest broad coagulation-disease framing available here. It also provides the strongest and most directly interpretable predictive evidence in the visible fields (PGS-only AUROC/R² plus full-model AUROC with CI) with a larger validation sample (n=67,425) and conventional covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). The alternatives (PGS001826, PGS002034) target a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency endpoint with a different EFO, and only report partial correlation (~0.056) rather than AUROC/R², making cross-candidate discrimination strength harder to compare; their covariate packaging is also slightly more elaborate (birth date, deprivation index). Between the two siblings, PGS002034 is a marginal runner-up over PGS001826 due to essentially identical partial-r but broader variant coverage, though neither is clearly better-supported than the direct-EFO match PGS001033. CRITIC: No clear mistake found. PGS001033 is the only candidate with trait_efo exactly matching the target (blood coagulation disease) and has directly interpretable predictive metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R² and full-model AUROC with CI) plus larger validation N (67,425) and conventional covariates. The alternatives (PGS001826/PGS002034) are for a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency endpoint with a different EFO and only report partial correlation (~0.056) without AUROC/R², making strength comparisons harder; nothing visible makes either clearly better-supported than the direct-EFO match. Legacy proposal and proposed_pick agree and are defensible, so keep legacy.

TRIAGE: All three candidates are direct-endpoint Crohn’s disease scores and should be compared head-to-head rather than filtered out.

- PGS004254 deserves close comparison because it reports much stronger apparent discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.72 with tight CI) and an effect size (OR 2.18), uses a very large genome-wide variant set (LDpred2-auto; 744,682 variants), and has a sizable European validation (n=22,296). However, its reported AUROC is full-model (not PRS-only), so a single-shot picker could be misled if covariates contribute materially; downstream comparison should explicitly check whether PRS-only performance is available elsewhere in the record set and how comparable the covariate packaging is.

- PGS001331 is a strong “clean-metric” comparator: it provides PRS-only AUROC/R² and full-model AUROC/R² with incremental AUROC, uses conventional covariates (age/sex/array/PCs), and has the same large UKB training scale (n=269,704) and validation size (n=24,905). It also slightly outperforms its sibling PGS001330 on the reported metrics, making it a plausible near-tie within the snpnet family.

- PGS001330 should remain in close comparison as the sibling alternative with a slightly different endpoint framing (time-to-event Crohn’s disease [regional enteritis]) and similarly clean PRS-only reporting. Even if slightly weaker on the headline metrics than PGS001331, endpoint definition differences (TTE vs non-TTE) can matter and could mislead a single-shot picker if ignored.

Net: shortlist all three to force an explicit comparison between (a) very strong but full-model-reported performance (PGS004254) and (b) cleaner PRS-only-reported UKB snpnet siblings with closely matched evaluation setup (PGS001331/PGS001330). Uncertainty: Key uncertainty is metric comparability: PGS004254’s AUROC is reported as full-model only (PRS-only not shown here), while PGS001330/PGS001331 provide PRS-only and incremental metrics. Without PRS-only AUROC for PGS004254, it’s unclear how much of the 0.72 is attributable to the score vs covariates, so downstream comparison should treat it as potentially strong but potentially non-comparable on a PRS-only axis. Another uncertainty is endpoint definition mismatch between PGS001330 (time-to-event regional enteritis framing) and the others (Crohn’s disease), which could affect apparent performance even within the same cohort family. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All three candidates are direct matches to Crohn’s disease (trait_efo = Crohn disease). PGS001330 is a time-to-event Crohn’s endpoint (phenotyping_reported indicates TTE), which is a mild endpoint mismatch versus a generic Crohn’s disease target; it also comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain knowledge flags as tending to generalize poorly. PGS001331 is the same framework family but with a straightforward Crohn’s disease phenotype and slightly better PRS-comparable metrics than PGS001330 (PGS-only AUROC 0.579 vs 0.576; PGS R² 0.00677 vs 0.00621), making it the stronger of the two framework siblings. PGS004254 has clean phenotype alignment (Crohn’s disease), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2-auto) with far more variants, and reports a strong effect size (OR 2.18) plus a high AUROC (0.72) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). However, the AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no PGS-only AUROC/R² reported), limiting comparability against the snpnet models’ explicit PGS-only metrics. Given the stronger structural signals and effect-size evidence with acceptable covariates, PGS004254 is preferred, but confidence is tempered by the lack of PRS-only discrimination metrics and the cross-study metric comparability issue. PICK: Keep the legacy proposal. All three candidates are direct matches to Crohn’s disease (trait_efo aligns; phenotyping is Crohn’s disease for PGS001331/PGS004254, and Crohn’s disease [regional enteritis] time-to-event for PGS001330). Between the two snpnet siblings, PGS001331 is the better-supported direct case/control-style Crohn’s disease score: slightly higher PGS-only AUROC/R² and higher full-model AUROC with similar covariates and identical training/validation scale, while PGS001330 has a mild endpoint framing mismatch (time-to-event) for a generic Crohn’s disease target.

PGS004254 remains the best-supported overall on visible predictive evidence despite less clean metric separation: it reports substantially stronger discrimination (AUROC 0.72 with tight CI) and a strong effect size (OR 2.18, tight CI) with conventional covariates (age/sex/PCs) and a large European validation sample (n=22,296). Although its AUROC is presented as a full-model metric (no PRS-only AUROC/R² shown here), the magnitude and precision of both AUROC and OR provide multiple independent signals of strong predictive performance that are not matched by the snpnet UKB pan-trait scores (PGS-only AUROC ~0.58; full-model AUROC ~0.61). This comparability caveat keeps confidence at Moderate and the outcome at DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL rather than DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY. CRITIC: No clear mistake found: all three candidates are direct matches to the target trait (Crohn disease) by trait_efo/trait_reported, with only PGS001330 showing a mild endpoint framing difference (time-to-event / regional enteritis). The proposed pick (PGS004254) is defensible on visible predictive evidence: it reports substantially higher discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.72, tight CI 0.70–0.73) and a strong effect size (OR 2.18, CI 2.05–2.32) with conventional covariates (age, sex, PCs) and a large EUR validation (n=22,296). While PRS-only metrics are not shown for PGS004254 (comparability caveat), the magnitude/precision of AUROC and OR provide stronger visible support than the snpnet UKB siblings (PGS-only AUROC ~0.576–0.579; full-model AUROC ~0.603–0.613). PGS001331 is a reasonable runner-up due to clean PRS-only reporting and slightly better metrics than PGS001330, but it is not clearly better-supported overall than PGS004254 given the visible performance gap. The legacy_with_domain_proposal also selects PGS004254 and is likewise defensible; since both legacy and proposed pick agree, keep_legacy_proposal=true and no revision is warranted.

TRIAGE: Two main publication families with multiple siblings merit head-to-head comparison.

1) 2024-12-16 Nat Genet family (PGS004946–PGS004951): keep multiple because they differ on endpoint wording ("Non-ischemic" vs "Clinical"), MTAG vs non-MTAG construction, validation ancestry (MAE-only vs EUR-only), and reported PRS-only metrics (univariate PRS-only AUC/AUPRC and delta R2 variants). Within this family, PGS004949 and PGS004951 look like the strongest/most competitive siblings on visible PRS-only AUC and effect size (and relatively larger delta metrics), but the endpoint/ancestry differences could make a single-shot pick misleading—so also keep near-ties PGS004947 and PGS004946 for direct comparison.

2) 2024-04-18 Nat Genet family (PGS004861–PGS004862): these are clean, direct "Dilated cardiomyopathy" labels with large EUR validation (n=347,585) and conventional covariates. Metrics are reported as full-model AUROC/R2/OR rather than clearly PRS-only, which can mislead comparisons versus the December family that reports explicit PRS-only AUC; nonetheless they are plausible strong baselines and should be compared head-to-head (especially PGS004862 vs PGS004861, where MTAG shows slightly higher AUROC/OR).

Watchlist: PGS004950 and PGS004948 are plausible but appear weaker than their closest siblings in the same December family on the visible PRS-only AUC/effect sizes and/or delta metrics; still keep them available because their endpoint label ("Clinical" vs "Non-ischemic") and validation setup differ and could matter depending on downstream endpoint matching priorities. Uncertainty: Comparability is limited by heterogeneous metric packaging: April records emphasize full-model AUROC/R2 with age/sex/PC covariates, while December records include explicit univariate PRS-only AUC/AUPRC plus multiple R2 definitions (Nagelkerke vs liability-scale, full vs delta). Endpoint fidelity also differs across December siblings ("Non-ischemic" vs "Clinical"), and validation ancestry differs (EUR-only vs MAE-only), so apparent performance differences may reflect cohort/endpoint composition rather than intrinsic score quality. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All 8 candidates are direct matches at the trait/EFO level (dilated cardiomyopathy), but they split into different endpoint packages: two models (PGS004861/PGS004862) use a generic DCM phenotype, while four models (PGS004946–PGS004949) are explicitly for non-ischemic DCM (a narrower subtype than the target), and two (PGS004950/PGS004951) are for clinical DCM but have much smaller validation sample size (n=7,761). Following the calibration preference for exact target-trait/phenotyping alignment, the generic DCM models are favored over the non-ischemic subtype models despite some siblings reporting higher PRS-only AUC/OR. Between the two generic DCM siblings from the same publication with identical covariates (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10) and evaluation ancestry (EUR), the MTAG-enhanced version (PGS004862) is mildly preferred per domain knowledge and also shows slightly stronger reported metrics (full-model AUROC 0.71 vs 0.70; OR 1.76 vs 1.56). Confidence is not high because the reported AUROCs for PGS004861/PGS004862 appear to be full-model (covariate-including) rather than clearly PRS-only, and several alternative models report explicit univariate (PRS-only) AUCs but on a narrower (non-ischemic) or different (clinical) endpoint, creating an unresolved comparability tradeoff. PICK: Keep the legacy proposal. All candidates are broadly direct at the trait/EFO level, but they differ materially in the phenotyping_reported endpoint. PGS004862 (and sibling PGS004861) are the only records whose reported phenotype is simply “Dilated cardiomyopathy” (matching the target without narrowing to a subtype), with conventional covariates (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10) and very large EUR validation (n=347,585). Although their reported discrimination is packaged as full-model AUROC/R2 (not explicitly PRS-only), the visible predictive evidence is still solid and comes from a large evaluation.

The December 2024 family contains models with stronger-looking PRS-only metrics (e.g., PGS004949 univariate AUC 0.68 and OR 1.91; PGS004951 univariate AUC 0.67 and OR 1.93), but these are tied to different endpoint packages (“Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy” for PGS004946–PGS004949; “Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy” for PGS004950–PGS004951) and/or much smaller validation N for the clinical endpoint (n=7,761 for PGS004951). Given the instruction to not revise away from the legacy pick unless an alternative is clearly better across multiple independent axes, the combination of closest endpoint wording + largest validation scale + ordinary covariate packaging keeps PGS004862 defensible as the best-supported direct-match.

Between the two April siblings, PGS004862 is preferred over PGS004861 because it is otherwise matched but shows consistently stronger visible performance (full-model AUROC 0.71 vs 0.70; R² 0.05 vs 0.048; OR 1.76 vs 1.56). CRITIC: No clear mistake found in the proposed_pick; it matches the legacy_with_domain_proposal and is defensible on visible evidence. Among candidates, PGS004861/PGS004862 are the only ones with phenotyping_reported exactly 'Dilated cardiomyopathy' (not narrowed to 'Non-ischemic' or shifted to 'Clinical'), and they have the largest validation sample size (n=347,585) with conventional covariates (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10). Although their metrics are packaged as full-model AUROC/R²/OR (not explicitly PRS-only), this is not a visible contradiction and remains usable evidence. Between the two April siblings, PGS004862 is consistently slightly stronger on the reported metrics (AUROC 0.71 vs 0.70; R² 0.05 vs 0.048; OR 1.76 vs 1.56), so preferring it over PGS004861 is supported. December-family alternatives (PGS004946–PGS004951) show explicit PRS-only AUC/OR that look stronger in places (e.g., PGS004949 AUC 0.68 OR 1.91; PGS004951 AUC 0.67 OR 1.93), but they come with endpoint shifts ('Non-ischemic' or 'Clinical') and/or much smaller validation N for the clinical endpoint (n=7,761), so they are not clearly better-supported for the target as stated. Therefore keep legacy proposal.

TRIAGE: Downstream comparison should center on (a) candidates with the strongest-looking direct-endpoint predictive evidence, while (b) preserving cleaner/alternative metric packages and near-ties that could flip under closer inspection of endpoint definition, metric type (PRS-only vs full-model), and cohort context.

Shortlist composition:
- High-performing CHF/heart-failure endpoint models with comparable reported discrimination in the same study family (HGG Adv MVP diverse-population comparison): PGS005077/PGS005083/PGS005076/PGS005074/PGS005080/PGS005084/PGS005078/PGS005085. These are near-tied on C-index (~0.75 range) and have strong ORs (~1.4–1.46). Because they are siblings with similar covariates (age/sex/PCs) and validation N (~31,804 EUR slice), they deserve head-to-head comparison rather than single-shot selection.
- Strong, cleanly reported PRS-only R2 plus full-model AUROC in a very large EUR validation (GBMI Cell Genom): PGS001790. Even though the AUROC is full-model, the presence of a PRS-only Nagelkerke R2 makes it a key “clean-metric” comparator against the MVP-family scores.
- Direct heart-failure endpoint with time-to-event framing (C-index + HR) and very large UKB validation: PGS000709. Metrics are not PRS-only and effect size is modest, but the survival setup and scale make it a potentially misleading under/over-performer if ignored.
- Recent multi-ancestry architecture paper with AUROC + Brier skill score (prevalent HF): PGS005097. Not PRS-only, but provides additional calibration-type evidence and a different training/validation context.
- Commun Biol “integration” family on ICD I50 HF with ORs (LDpred2 vs metaPRS): PGS004462 and PGS004532. Metrics are sparse (OR only; covariates unknown), but they are direct I50 HF endpoints and could look deceptively strong/weak depending on how OR was computed; keep for explicit scrutiny.

Watchlist composition (plausible alternatives / could mislead):
- PGS003969 (39 SNP GWS; OR reported; covariates unknown): direct HF label but sparse model; could look attractive due to simplicity/OR yet underperform vs genome-wide models.
- Remaining MVP HGG Adv siblings with lower C-index/OR (PGS005073/PGS005079/PGS005082/PGS005075/PGS005081): same family and endpoint, but appear weaker; still useful as internal baselines and to avoid cherry-picking.
- NPJ Genom Med LDpred2 family (PGS005299–PGS005306): direct HF label but notably lower AUROC (~0.57–0.63) and small dev/training Ns in some; could mislead if someone overweights recency or variant count.
- UKB portability “partial-r” CHF/pulmonary heart disease scores (PGS001842/PGS002051/PGS001840/PGS002049): adjacent endpoints (congestive HF subtype; pulmonary heart disease) and different metric (partial correlation) with small validation N (~20k); could be mistakenly compared directly to AUROC/C-index without careful normalization.
- Context-specific incident HF in special cohorts (PGS004598 breast cancer survivors; PGS005319 medication-treated cohort): HRs reported but endpoints/populations are specialized and could mislead if treated as general-population HF predictors. Uncertainty: Key uncertainties that warrant downstream close comparison rather than early filtering: (1) many top-looking candidates report full-model discrimination (AUROC/C-index) rather than PRS-only, so apparent superiority may reflect covariate packaging differences; (2) endpoint heterogeneity (heart failure vs congestive HF phecode vs ICD I50 vs prevalent vs incident vs subtype/special cohorts) could dominate performance differences; (3) within the MVP HGG Adv family, multiple near-tied scores differ mainly by method label, and the visible metadata doesn’t expose enough to safely pick one without a deliberate sibling comparison. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: Multiple direct-match heart-failure PRS candidates are present. PGS001790 is preferred because it has exact trait/phenotype alignment (Heart failure), reports a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke’s R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.006981), and is evaluated in a large European sample (n=358,905) with only demographic/PC-style covariates (age/sex terms, 20 PCs), reducing concern that performance is driven by heavy clinical packaging. However, the evidence remains sub-optimal because the headline AUROC=0.75 appears to be a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only), and several other direct-match candidates report effect sizes (e.g., OR=1.28 for PGS003969; multiple CHF PheCode models with higher C-index/OR) but differ in endpoint framing (prevalent vs incident vs CHF phecode) and lack clearly comparable PRS-only metrics, preventing a high-confidence, clearly dominant choice from the visible metadata alone. PICK: Keep the legacy proposal (PGS001790) because, among the direct-match heart-failure-labeled candidates, it remains the most defensible on multiple independent visible axes simultaneously: (1) direct endpoint alignment (trait/phenotyping both heart failure), (2) uniquely provides a PRS-comparable metric (PGS-only Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.006981) rather than only full-model discrimination/effect sizes, (3) very large European validation sample (n=358,905) with conventional demographic/PC covariates (age/sex terms + PCs) that reduces concern that performance is dominated by heavy clinical packaging, and (4) broad multi-cohort training context (GBMI-style aggregation) consistent with robust polygenic signal capture.

Several alternatives look strong but do not clearly dominate PGS001790 across endpoint-directness plus overall predictive evidence quality as visible here. The MVP HGG Adv CHF PheCode family (e.g., PGS005083/PGS005077/PGS005076/PGS005074) shows higher reported C-index (~0.753) and strong ORs (~1.45), but these are for a CHF phecode endpoint (not exactly the target label), are reported as full-model C-index with covariates (age/sex/PCs) rather than PRS-only metrics, and are validated in a much smaller EUR slice (n=31,804), making it hard to justify a clear revision away from the legacy pick based on the metadata alone. Other direct HF candidates are either weaker on visible discrimination (e.g., NPJ Genom Med AUROC ~0.57–0.63), sparse/unclear on covariates and metrics (e.g., OR-only records like PGS004462/PGS004532; covariates unknown), specialized populations (PGS004598 breast cancer survivors; PGS005319 medication cohort), or show modest effect in a survival model despite large N (PGS000709 HR~1.08; C-index 0.635).

Thus, while the choice remains sub-optimal due to heterogeneous endpoint framing across candidates and because PGS001790’s AUROC=0.75 appears to be a full-model metric, no alternative is clearly better-supported across multiple independent visible axes strongly enough to overturn the legacy proposal. CRITIC: No clear mistake found in the proposed_pick: PGS001790 is a direct heart-failure record (trait/phenotyping both Heart failure), has very large EUR validation (n=358,905), conventional covariates, and uniquely reports a PRS-only metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.006981) alongside a full-model AUROC=0.75. The main competing family (PGS005074/076/077/078/080/083/084/085 etc.) targets a CHF PheCode endpoint (not exactly the same label), reports full-model C-index (~0.75) and ORs (~1.4–1.46) with smaller EUR validation (n=31,804), and lacks PRS-only separation in the visible metadata—so it is not a clearly better-supported alternative that would force revision. Other direct HF candidates either have weaker visible discrimination (e.g., PGS000709 C-index 0.635; NPJ Genom Med AUROC ~0.57–0.63), sparse/unclear metric packaging (OR-only with unknown covariates: PGS004462/PGS004532), or specialized cohorts (PGS004598, PGS005319). Legacy_with_domain_proposal also selects PGS001790 and remains defensible; since both legacy and proposed_pick agree, keep_legacy_proposal=true.

TRIAGE: Shortlist focuses on candidates with (a) direct hip OA / coxarthrosis endpoint alignment and (b) at least one interpretable predictive signal (AUC/C-index/HR/OR) plus enough context (covariates, validation N) to support head-to-head comparison.

- PGS000967: Direct hip OA/cxarthrosis TTE phenotype; provides both PRS-only and full-model metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.56; incremental AUROC reported) with conventional covariates and decent validation N. Also includes multi-ancestry eval distribution (though selected performance is EUR), making it a key anchor for metric cleanliness and endpoint fidelity.
- PGS002728: Hip OA framed via a strong clinical proxy endpoint (total hip replacement) with full-model AUROC ~0.66 (age/sex). Metrics are not PRS-only, but the endpoint is closely aligned and performance is competitive enough that it could beat “cleaner” but weaker PRS-only candidates; deserves direct comparison.
- PGS004882: Incident hip OA with very large validation N and time-to-event style reporting (C-index ~0.60; HR ~1.4). Even though training N is small/atypical and PRS-only metrics aren’t separated, the scale + incident endpoint + reported discrimination make it a plausible near-tie and a potential “looks modest but robust” contender.
- PGS002763: Direct hip OA endpoint with a strong effect-size summary (OR ~1.38) and large validation N. Lacks AUC/C-index, but the reported association strength and modern genome-wide method make it a plausible competitor that could be undervalued by a single-shot picker focused only on AUC availability.

Watchlist retains candidates that could mislead selection if taken at face value (e.g., missing covariate/metric context, sibling-method ambiguity, or very limited validation), but still might win downstream depending on what PICK prioritizes.
- PGS004478 vs PGS004548: Same publication family, same endpoint label (M16 coxarthrosis) and same variant count; only ORs reported and covariates are unknown. They are plausible but hard to compare fairly without more performance context; keep both to avoid prematurely choosing the wrong sibling.
- PGS002750: Endpoint is hip replacement (aligned proxy) but validation N is small and only an OR is provided with a relatively rich covariate set (BMI/education/SES etc.), which complicates comparability; could look better/worse depending on packaging and should not be dropped entirely.

Overall downstream comparison should explicitly separate: (1) PRS-only vs full-model metrics (PGS000967 as the clean comparator), (2) endpoint differences (incident hip OA vs coxarthrosis vs replacement proxy), and (3) scale/robustness signals (validation N, method/variant breadth) so that candidates with strong direct-endpoint evidence but imperfect metric packaging are not accidentally discarded. Uncertainty: Several candidates lack PRS-only discrimination metrics (AUC/C-index) and/or have only OR/HR without clear standardization, making cross-candidate comparability uncertain. PGS004882’s unusually small training N (with huge validation N) could reflect a specific modeling setup not visible here. The Commun Biol siblings (PGS004478/PGS004548) have unknown covariates and only single-point ORs, so their apparent performance could be misleading in either direction. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All 7 candidates are direct matches at the EFO level (osteoarthritis, hip), but they differ materially in endpoint fidelity and comparability. PGS002763 has the cleanest phenotype alignment to the target as reported (phenotyping_reported: "Hip osteoarthritis"), uses only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs/technical), and provides a reasonably strong PRS effect size (OR 1.38 per SD; moderate signal). Key limitations are that it reports no PRS-comparable AUROC/R², and several competitors have endpoint packaging concerns: PGS002728 and PGS002750 are based on hip replacement/total hip replacement (procedure-defined advanced disease) with additional covariates in PGS002750; PGS000967 is a pan-trait UKB sparse framework score with time-to-event phenotyping and modest PRS-only AUROC (~0.56), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused scores; PGS004478/PGS004548 have unknown covariates and only single-point ORs; PGS004882 is incident-only and appears embedded in an absolute-incidence framework with only a full-model C-index reported. Given missing comparable discrimination metrics for the best-aligned disease-endpoint models and mixed endpoint packaging across the pool, the direct-match choice is supported but not high-certainty. PICK: Keep the legacy proposal. Across the full candidate list, PGS002763 remains the most defensible direct-match for the target trait based on endpoint fidelity plus strength/scale of the visible association evidence.

- Endpoint alignment: PGS002763 is explicitly phenotyped as “Hip osteoarthritis” (not a procedure proxy like replacement/arthroplasty, and not a broader/alternate framing). Several others are still direct at EFO, but have endpoint packaging differences (e.g., PGS002728/PGS002750 use hip replacement/total hip replacement; PGS000967 is a UKB pan-trait TTE coxarthrosis construct; PGS004882 is incident-only).
- Predictive/effect evidence: PGS002763 reports a relatively strong and well-bounded effect size (OR 1.38, 95% CI 1.31–1.46). Competing OR-only candidates are weaker or less well-specified (PGS004478 OR ~1.30 with unknown covariates; PGS004548 OR ~1.22; PGS002750 OR 1.23 with small validation N).
- Validation scale and conventional covariates: PGS002763 has a large European validation sample (n=39,444) and uses ordinary covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical), supporting interpretability and reducing concerns that performance is driven by unusual packaging.

Why not switch:
- PGS000967 has the cleanest PRS-only AUROC/R² reporting, but its PRS-only discrimination is modest (AUROC ~0.56) and it is a pan-trait UKB sparse score; it is a strong runner-up anchor for metric cleanliness, but not clearly better overall than PGS002763 on visible predictive signal.
- PGS004882 has huge validation N and reports HR ~1.4 / C-index ~0.60, but the training sample size shown is atypically small (n=404) and metrics are not clearly PRS-only; this makes it hard to justify as clearly superior to the legacy pick.
- PGS002728 reports full-model AUROC ~0.66 (age/sex) but uses a procedure-defined endpoint (“Total hip replacement”), which is a materially different construct than hip osteoarthritis itself; not clearly better-supported for the target trait.

Given no alternative is clearly better across multiple independent visible axes (endpoint fidelity + strength of evidence + comparability/packaging), retaining PGS002763 is warranted, with moderate confidence due to missing AUC/C-index for that record. CRITIC: No clear mistake found in the proposed pick: PGS002763 is a direct hip osteoarthritis phenotype (phenotyping_reported: "Hip osteoarthritis"), has a sizeable EUR validation sample (n=39,444), conventional covariates, and a relatively strong reported association (OR 1.38, 95% CI 1.31–1.46). Therefore keep the legacy proposal and the proposed pick as-is.

TRIAGE: All candidates are nominally direct-endpoint (ulcerative colitis) but come from two distinct study families with different metric packaging.

Shortlist (close downstream comparison):
- PGS001306 (snpnet; 179 variants): Direct endpoint with clean PRS-only metrics reported (PGS-only AUROC 0.630; full-model AUROC 0.662 with conventional covariates). Solid validation N (24,905) and explicit covariates make it a strong “clean-metric” baseline.
- PGS001307 (snpnet; 809 variants; time-to-event phenotype): Same publication family as PGS001306 but different endpoint framing (TTE). Has clean PRS-only AUROC (0.638) and large validation N (67,425). This can look better/worse depending on whether downstream PICK prioritizes strict endpoint match vs robustness/scale; it’s a classic near-tie sibling that could mislead a single-shot picker if endpoint differences are ignored.
- PGS004253 (LDpred2-auto; 744,575 variants): Direct endpoint with strong-looking reported effects (OR 1.84) and AUROC 0.66 (with covariates listed). Despite smaller training (n=13,382) and smaller validation N (5,735), it is the most recent and has comparatively strong apparent predictive signal; however, metrics are not clearly separated into PRS-only vs full-model, so it needs head-to-head scrutiny against the snpnet siblings rather than being accepted at face value.

Watchlist (plausible alternatives / potentially misleading evidence):
- PGS001855 (penalized regression bigstatsr; 1,505 variants): Same portability paper family as PGS002066; reports partial correlation (partial-r 0.0625) rather than AUROC/R2, making direct comparison tricky. Could be competitive but metric type mismatch can mislead; keep for downstream reconciliation.
- PGS002066 (LDpred2; 566,637 variants): Reports AUROC 0.57 and OR 1.11 with “covariates: Unknown,” which raises interpretability/comparability uncertainty (PRS-only vs full-model unclear; packaging unclear). Large variant count and same portability context make it worth retaining as a comparator, but it is not the strongest on visible predictive evidence.

Overall, downstream comparison should explicitly separate: (i) snpnet siblings with clean PRS-only AUROC/R2 and conventional covariates, (ii) the newer LDpred2-auto UC score with strong-looking OR/AUROC but less clean metric separation, and (iii) portability-paper scores with non-comparable or under-specified metric packaging. Uncertainty: Key uncertainties are (1) endpoint comparability between standard case/control UC (PGS001306/PGS004253) and TTE UC (PGS001307), (2) whether PGS004253’s AUROC/OR reflect PRS-only vs covariate-augmented performance (despite covariates being listed), and (3) metric-type mismatch/under-specification in the portability-paper records (partial-r for PGS001855; unknown covariates and unclear packaging for PGS002066), which can distort naive ranking. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All 5 candidates are direct matches to ulcerative colitis by trait_reported/trait_efo, but they differ in endpoint packaging and evidence quality. PGS004253 has the cleanest direct phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: Ulcerative colitis) and is from a disease-focused UC paper (Nat Commun) rather than a pan-trait sparse framework (PGS001306/PGS001307) or a UKB portability sweep (PGS001855/PGS002066). It also reports comparatively strong discrimination/effect evidence in the visible record (AUROC 0.66 with CI 0.64–0.68; OR 1.84 per SD with tight CI) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), avoiding heavy clinical packaging. Main limitation: the validation sample size is relatively small (n=5,735) and the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² shown), reducing comparability versus the snpnet models that do report PGS-only metrics; therefore confidence is not high despite the strong effect-size signal. PICK: Keep the legacy proposal (PGS004253). All candidates are direct-label matches to ulcerative colitis, but none is so clearly superior across multiple independent visible axes that it justifies revising away from PGS004253.

PGS004253 remains defensible as best-supported on visible predictive signal while staying endpoint-direct: it reports UC directly (trait/phenotyping) with conventional covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and shows the strongest apparent association/discrimination in-record (AUROC 0.66 with tight CI 0.64–0.68; OR 1.84 with tight CI). Although its training/validation sizes are smaller (train n=13,382; validation n=5,735) and the AUROC appears to be a covariate-including metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R²), the magnitude/precision of the reported effect and AUROC are strong enough that the cleaner metric separation of the UKB pan-trait snpnet siblings does not clearly outweigh it.

The main alternatives:
- PGS001306 is a strong runner-up: direct UC endpoint, clear PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.630; full-model AUROC 0.662) and larger validation (n=24,905). However, its PRS-only discrimination is lower than PGS004253’s reported AUROC, and nothing else in the visible record makes it clearly better overall.
- PGS001307 has slightly higher PRS-only AUROC (0.638) and very large validation (n=67,425), but its endpoint is explicitly time-to-event UC, making it less strictly aligned than the direct case/control UC framing of PGS004253/PGS001306.

The portability-paper scores (PGS001855 partial-r only; PGS002066 AUROC 0.57 with unknown covariates and weak OR) are not competitive on visible predictive evidence/interpretability.

Therefore, PGS004253 stays best, but outcome remains DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL due to metric-packaging ambiguity (PRS-only vs full-model) and smaller validation scale. CRITIC: No clear mistake found: all candidates are direct-label matches to ulcerative colitis, and the proposed/legacy pick (PGS004253) is defensible on visible evidence. PGS004253 shows the strongest in-record predictive signal (AUROC 0.66, CI 0.64–0.68; OR 1.84, CI 1.76–1.93) with conventional covariates listed (age, sex, array, PCs) and direct phenotyping_reported=Ulcerative colitis. The main downside—metrics appear to be full-model only (no explicit PRS-only AUC/R2) and smaller validation N (5,735)—is acknowledged and does not create a visible contradiction.

Alternatives are not clearly better-supported: PGS001306 has clean PRS-only metrics and larger validation N (24,905) but lower PRS-only AUROC (0.630) and similar full-model AUROC (0.662) without stronger effect-size evidence. PGS001307 has large validation N (67,425) and PRS-only AUROC 0.638 but is explicitly time-to-event UC, making endpoint alignment less strict than PGS004253’s direct UC framing. PGS001855 reports only partial-r (0.0625) and PGS002066 shows weaker AUROC (0.57) with unknown covariates and OR CI crossing 1, so neither is better-supported.

Because the proposed_pick matches the legacy_with_domain_proposal and both are defensible, keep_legacy_proposal=true and no revision.
